name: Nolan
issues: Surname collision merges two characters: 'Nolan' (Zane's uncle Nolan Lowell, Eps 8-21) and 'Alan Nolan' (vice leader of the Dragonblaze Hall, Eps 447-448, verified in episode text). The Ep 447-448 mentions belong to the separate character Alan Nolan, not the uncle.
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Nolan' was chosen for Zane's powerful antagonist uncle, with the surname 'Lowell' tying him into Zane's family unit; the best-fitting source candidate in the aligned chapters is Zane's third uncle Luo Junyi, who presides over the early deathmatch, though the second uncle (Luo Bingquan) is also possible.
description: Zane's uncle and an early family antagonist (Eps 8-21). A cultivator far beyond mere Marrow Refining, he seizes the forge by its rim as Zane vanishes inside it, and even his formidable power is not enough to intimidate Jace on Zane's behalf. Per the master sheet he is an antagonist within the Lowell family.

name: Initiate Adept
reason: The show's Adept Realm localizes the source's Xiantian realm; 'Initiate Adept' renders its entry level in the Western fantasy register instead of a literal 'Xiantian stage one'.
description: The entry level of the Adept Realm, the cultivation stage above Marrow Refining. Dustin and Rhys are Initiate Adepts, and Zane launched a soul attack on a Fourth-level Adept while still a mere Initiate Adept fueling his fists with Raw Vitality. Wyatt reaches this level around Ep 165.

name: Brenda
issues: MasterLS note calls her 'Helen's friend', using the abandoned 'Helen' localization for Ingrid; the delivered episodes consistently use Ingrid (Eps 196, 207).
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Brenda' was chosen as a friendly, everyday feminine name for Mo Yun, the Maiden's Peak disciple who is Yates's cousin and Ingrid's best friend.
description: A Maiden's Peak disciple, Yates's cousin and Ingrid's best friend (and James's niece). At Yates's request she persistently persuaded Ingrid to attend the estate party in Eps 195-196. Matches source Mo Yun, Mo Yu's cousin who dragged Zhu Qianning over from Jade Maiden Peak.

name: Level Two Adept
reason: Sub-level of the Adept Realm, which localizes the source's Xiantian realm; 'Level Two Adept' renders the Xiantian second stage in the show's tier naming.
description: The second sub-level of the Adept Realm. Jacob cracked the top one hundred of the Sect rankings while only a Level Two Adept, and opponents at this level are considered easy prey for stronger fighters.

name: Black Lotus Karmafire
reason: Source term 'Green Lotus Hellfire' (Pei Tianyao's flame) was localized as 'Black Lotus Karmafire', recoloring the flame and swapping 'Hellfire' for the more evocative 'Karmafire' in the Western fantasy register.
description: Patrick's signature hellish flame, described as the definition of hell on earth, impossibly powerful and indefensible; its only desire is to burn everything down. It can split into larger and smaller flames, and even Frank, confident of shattering Patrick's Form of the Adamant Soul, knows he could never withstand it. Corresponds to Pei Tianyao's Green Lotus Hellfire in the source.

name: Blood Drinker
reason: The source weapon name 'Blooddrinker' was kept nearly verbatim, split into two words as 'Blood Drinker' for readability.
description: A middle-grade Mythic Weapon sword that catches the light with a red flash, chosen by Zane around Ep 323. After a puppet ripped his Streamer to pieces, Zane fought with Blood Drinker as his main blade, leaving his sword spirit Lily without a weapon; he wields it with the Apex of Sword Intent. Mirrors source Blooddrinker, which Luo Zheng used after the Sword of Flowing Light was destroyed.

name: Level Three Adept
reason: Sub-level of the Adept Realm, which localizes the source's Xiantian realm; the source's 'Xiantian third stage' is rendered as 'Level Three Adept' in the show's tier naming.
description: The third sub-level of the Adept Realm. Opponents condescend to Zane for being only a Level Three Adept during the trials around Eps 326-386, matching the source's 'little Xiantian third stage disciple'.

name: Dragon Lineage
reason: The source's 'Dragon Bloodline Clan' was localized as the 'True Dragon Lineage' to read as a noble dragon dynasty in the Western fantasy register.
description: The clan of true dragons to which the Cobalt Dragon belongs. Because many dragon-blooded races lived in the Lower World, the True Dragon Lineage built Dragon Soar Arenas to transport their own to the upper world (source: the Dragon Bloodline Clan and its Rising Dragon Arenas).

name: Orange Sea Realm
reason: The source term 'Orange Sea Realm' was carried over verbatim; it already fit the adaptation's fantasy register.
description: A vast outer realm whose boundless starry sky hosts a major expedition for the top talents of the Thirteen Palaces (Eps 1067-1110). Ages ago a cataclysmic war between several Supreme Lords nearly tore the entire realm apart, and a giant 'Seal' character can cut areas off from the realm outside. Verified verbatim in the source around chapter 1075.

name: Abner
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Abner' was chosen as an old-fashioned, rough-edged name for Hou Da, the desperate survivor of the insect-swarm tunnel.
description: A warrior trapped in the dark tunnels during the swarm attack of Eps 1132-1141, swearing at a sealed door and even shoving a man into the gathering swarm to save himself. He is saved at the last moment by the Saint Lord from the Magnolia Sanctum and later travels on with Lincoln and Freya. Matches source Hou Da, who cursed in the darkness as the Black Eating Moths killed his brothers one by one before experts from the Yulan Holy Land rescued him.

name: Magic Vision
reason: The source reward 'Clear Eyes Spirit Eyes' was renamed 'Magic Vision' as a cleaner, more natural English name for the eye ability.
description: An eye ability Zane gains in Ep 547 when a mystical sap rejuvenates his eyes, chosen over a reward of five hundred years of lifespan at the Cobalt Dragon's urging. It manifests as a green light hidden deep in his pupils and lets him see through most illusions, concealment and assassination techniques, though strange fog can still blunt it. Matches the source's Clear Eyes Spirit Eyes reward explained by Qinglong.

name: Sacred Race
reason: Source term 'Sacred Clan' was localized as 'Sacred Race', swapping 'Clan' for 'Race' in line with the show's naming of peoples.
description: A supreme race described as the creators of laws. Gus carries the bloodline of a king from the Sacred Race, and its elites are powerhouses at the Spirit Sea Realm and beyond.

name: Teleportation Token
reason: The source's English term 'Teleportation Token' was carried over verbatim.
description: A treasure Zane obtains from the giant Gilded Warden around Ep 1223 that teleports him instantly to another location, dissolving the world around him. Each activation is followed by a long recharge cooldown, so Zane rations its use carefully while hopping between locations in the Illusion Battlefield.

name: White
issues: Not a single entity: standalone 'White' folds together fragments of several names - 'White Bone Armor' and Frank's 'White Spear' (per masterls) and 'the Woman in White', a female guide character appearing only in Eps 1261-1263 (verified by episode search).
reason: Dropped as a fragment token; its mentions belong to distinct White-prefixed entities rather than one entity.

name: Laney
reason: The adaptation gave Sloane's second body a distinct personal name, 'Laney', echoing Sloane's own name; in the source this duplicate is known by the epithet 'Black Snow', hence the black snow that falls around Laney instead of Sloane's white.
description: A second version of Sloane fighting her own battles in another upper world of the Illusion Battlefield (Eps 1239-1241); black snow drifts around her where white snow surrounds Sloane. The two bodies share one soul and cultivate separately, and once merged Sloane will become a complete, far stronger existence. Matches source 'Black Snow', the second body of Ji Luoxue who entered the Illusory Battlefield under two identities.

name: Xander
reason: The character's Chinese Daoist name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Xander' was chosen as an authoritative-sounding name for the elder who commands the Ethereal Spirit Sect contingent.
description: The authority over the Ethereal Spirit Sect disciples at the Martial Tournament (Ep 487), known for enforcing discipline and decorum - he snaps Brent back into line - and for his analytical mind. He remains a respected power into the later arcs, a man even Maddox knows better than to underestimate (Ep 697). Likely corresponds to Taoist Priest Qing Xu, the old-fashioned backbone of the Void Spirit Sect who keeps its disciples in check at the source's Martial Arts Conference.

name: Edgar
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Edgar Sinclair' was chosen as a refined, aristocratic name for the Ethereal Spirit Sect duelist, matching the sect's elevated status.
description: An Ethereal Spirit Sect disciple at Inner-Core Realm who fights Blake of Cloud Hall in the tournament (Eps 487-489). Gracious in defeat, he concedes with 'You win' while noting Blake would not have beaten him so easily off that stage. Likely corresponds to Situ Haoran of the Void Spirit Sect, who faces a Cloud Hall champion in the matching source duel.

name: Fourth-Grade
reason: The source's sect-ranking term 'fourth grade sect' was carried over as 'Fourth-Grade Sect' (also phrased 'Fourth-Grade Order' in some episodes).
description: A rank in the sect-grading system of The Heartlands, a status held by only a few powers such as the Cloud Hall itself, the Bloodwood Cliff, and the Mysterious Luna Hall (Ep 717). Possessing a top treasure can instantly elevate a clan to Fourth-Grade status, and Fourth-Grade sects queue for Zane's arrays. Matches the source's fourth grade sect ranking (e.g. 'the fourth grade sect Cloud Hall').

name: Gregory
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Gregory' was chosen as a solid, established-sounding name for the Crystal Martial House's champion.
description: The top warrior of the Crystal Martial House at the Spirit-Tribulation Realm (Eps 788-805), whose heart hammers when he measures Zane's strength. He was considered one of only two real contenders for the First Tier alongside Edwin, but falls out of the running by Ep 803. Matches source Zhan Yun, the number one False Tribulation Realm warrior of the Black Jade Martial House, in a near-verbatim scene.

name: Willard
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Willard' was chosen as a slightly old-fashioned name for the nimble duelist famed for his speed.
description: A fighter in the Martial House tournament famed for his speed and incredible agility (Eps 802-803). Challenged to survive three strikes, he dodges by a hair - the Spatial Blade tears a huge gash in his robe - then shouts 'Three strikes!' in pure joy at having outlasted them. Matches source Yue Congyun, who evades Yun Longtao's promised three strikes rather than face him head-on.

name: Spectral Plains
reason: The island's vengeful-spirit region (the source's Spirit Beast Area / Spiritual Beast District) was renamed 'The Spectral Plains' to fit the Western fantasy register.
description: A haunted region on the expedition island (Eps 843-846) that lies before the island's center; something there can call forth more spectral beasts to attack travelers. Corresponds to the source's spirit-beast district where vengeful spirits mass in the sky and Vengeful Spirit Beasts crush bound warriors.

name: Crystal Coffin
reason: The source's English term 'crystal coffin' was carried over verbatim as a proper item name.
description: A chained coffin suspended within a stone pillar (Eps 895-901) that cannot be broken open or freed from its chains. The woman sealed alone inside it for years has been changed by the isolation. Matches the crystal coffin in which Feng Nianyun is chained and sealed by the Soul Sealing Technique in the source.

name: Scribe
reason: The source's 'Book Immortal', the familiar who manages the library, was localized as 'The Scribe', a title fitting the Western fantasy register.
description: The keeper of the ancient library (Eps 984-987), an old spirit who guides visitors through its memoirs and sealed books and is shocked by Zane's successive revelations. Even Saul, who never concedes ground to the Scribe, defers to his judgment about the sealed method. Matches the source's Book Immortal, the library familiar who bickers with Afo and teaches Luo Zheng to pour his perception into the books.

name: Sunbelt
reason: An adaptation-named region; no matching source location appears in the evidence, so 'The Sunbelt' appears to be an invented Western-style name for the Razorwing swarm territory.
description: A region known as Razorwing swarm territory (Eps 61-136), reachable by Skycruiser in a single day. Outer Disciples take contracts there to handle Razor swarms.

name: Corbin Blackwood
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Corbin' was chosen for Zhang Wuji, with the surname 'Blackwood' shared with his younger brother Dustin to keep House Blackwood a consistent family unit.
description: Dustin Blackwood's older brother of House Blackwood, who runs The Gilded Gavel auction house (Eps 101-102). He waives the house's usual ten percent commission for Zane as Dustin's friend and watches the young man with curiosity and anticipation. Matches source Zhang Wuji, Zhang Wuxian's older brother at the Tianlu Auction House, in a near-verbatim commission scene.

name: Phoenix Gem
reason: The source item 'Fire Scorpion Crystal Core' was renamed 'Phoenix Gem', trading the literal beast-part name for a more evocative treasure name in the Western fantasy register.
description: A rare treasure Zane puts up for auction through Dustin at The Gilded Gavel (Eps 96-102), fetching seventy thousand Crystal Cubes to the disbelief of Ethan and others. Matches the source's Fire Scorpion Crystal Core, which sold for exactly 70,000 square crystals at the Tianlu Auction.

name: Hazel
issues: Episode pronoun signal is noisy (m9/f6), but her episode contexts ('her fee', 'her brow') and the source counterpart (Miss Qing Ling, a female singer) are unambiguously female.
reason: The character's Chinese stage name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Hazel' was chosen as a soft, graceful name for the celebrated songstress.
description: A celebrated singer and the grill's headliner (Eps 102-103), whose fee is astronomical; her attendance is personally arranged as a mark of honor for Zane's party. She performs with a dancer's grace until something repugnant makes her stop mid-song. Corresponds to Miss Qing Ling, the famed songstress invited to sing for Luo Zheng's gathering in the source.

name: Dragon Valley
reason: The source's English place name 'Dragon Valley' was carried over verbatim.
description: A secluded valley Zane seeks out eagerly (Eps 109-167), lying just behind a landmark he is directed to. When he moves through Dragon Valley he does not see another soul, and a noble-clan Adept there was later disintegrated into dust by the power of his stars. Verified verbatim in source chapters ~128-136.

name: Payne
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Payne' was chosen as a wry, memorable surname-style name for the gruff, mercenary healer.
description: A gruff healer at The Crucible (Eps 122-123) notorious for quoting astronomical prices - he once let a man bleed out over his fee. He nonetheless spends six grueling hours saving Zane's life, emerging drenched in sweat to a waiting Ingrid, and is intrigued by the strangeness of Zane's wounds. Matches source Zhu Feihang of the golden-needle Zhu Family, who saves Luo Zheng with the Great Yin Yang Golden Needles while Zhu Qianning waits.
